## Laboratory 04 - Step 1/4

### Add a valid case and an intended CIDR rejection

| Before you begin | This step |
| --- | --- |
| Goal | Set up this independent copy and add two real learner tests to its already-complete baseline. |
| Time | 30–40 minutes including first-time setup and the first focused test run. |
| Files | Edit [tests/learner.tftest.hcl](../../tests/learner.tftest.hcl) using [exercises/learner-test.tftest.hcl.example](../../exercises/learner-test.tftest.hcl.example); keep module code unchanged. |
| Starting branch | Your own copy's actual default branch, normally `dev`; create `lab/tests-docs`. |

Beginner guides: [Start here](../../docs/start-here.md) · [Git workflow](../../docs/git-workflow.md) · [Copilot guide](../../docs/copilot-guide.md) · [Toolchain](../../docs/toolchain.md) · [Troubleshooting](../../docs/troubleshooting.md).

> [!NOTE]
> No previous repository is required. The complete network baseline, security child, input validations, locks, and provider mocks are included.
> Work on tests and documentation, not a replacement implementation. Use Cmd+P, Cmd+S, Cmd+Shift+P, and the Source Control icon on macOS.

### 1. Create your own private copy in the browser

1. Sign in to GitHub, inspect the profile-picture menu, and verify your invited personal account and permitted repository owner.
2. Open [alvinea28/ws2-terraform-tests-docs-laboratory-04](https://github.com/alvinea28/ws2-terraform-tests-docs-laboratory-04).
3. Select **COPY EXERCISE**, or **Use this template** → **Create a new repository**.
4. Choose the authorized **Owner**, a unique name ending in `laboratory-04`, and **Private**; leave **Include all branches** unchecked.
5. Select **Create repository**, verify your new owner/name and **Private** badge, and wait for the initial automation.
6. Refresh the landing page and open its **Exercise** link, or find the existing Exercise under **Issues**; do not edit public-template files.

### 2. Clone and open this copy in desktop VS Code

1. In **your copy**, select **Code** → **HTTPS** and copy the credential-free clone URL.
2. Press **Ctrl+Shift+P** in desktop VS Code, select **Git: Clone**, paste **your own copy URL**, and press **Enter**.
3. For an expected authorization prompt, select **Allow**, check the correct GitHub personal account in the browser, and authorize the recognized VS Code request.
4. Return through **Open Visual Studio Code**; complete Git Credential Manager's separate trusted browser sign-in if it appears.
5. Choose a local **parent folder**, select **Select as Repository Destination**, then **Open** after cloning completes.
6. Trust only this known-source clone. Check **Explorer** opens the clone itself, not a parent/multi-repo workspace, public template, ZIP, or `github.dev`.
7. Correct a wrong folder through **File** → **Open Folder...** before editing or opening a terminal.

### 3. Check accounts, tool versions, and the doctor before branching

1. Open VS Code **Accounts** and verify the intended GitHub personal account separately from browser sign-in.
2. Use **Sign in with GitHub to use GitHub Copilot** if needed; select the Copilot account through **Manage Extension Account Preferences...**.
3. Confirm the assigned Copilot seat/entitlement with the instructor, and complete [local authorship setup](../../docs/start-here.md#set-authorship-only-for-this-repository).
4. Select **Terminal** → **New Terminal** at this clone's root and run each line separately:

```powershell
node --version
terraform version
terraform-docs version
node scripts/doctor.mjs
```

Expect Node **24.16.0**, Terraform **1.16.1**, terraform-docs **0.24.0**, and the supplied AzureRM **5.4.0** requirement/lock.
Resolve every doctor `CHECK`; it cannot certify browser authorization, a Copilot seat, or push rights. A missing doctor means an incomplete package, not a pass.

### 4. Create the branch and transfer the supplied starter

1. Press **Ctrl+Shift+G**, verify this repository and a clean working tree, select the actual default branch, normally `dev`, then **...** → **Pull**.
2. Press **Ctrl+Shift+P** → **Git: Create Branch...**, enter `lab/tests-docs`, and press **Enter**; verify the status-bar branch, or select it if it already exists.
3. Press **Ctrl+P** → [exercises/learner-test.tftest.hcl.example](../../exercises/learner-test.tftest.hcl.example); read it, then use **Ctrl+A**, **Ctrl+C** to copy its complete content.
4. Press **Ctrl+P** → [tests/learner.tftest.hcl](../../tests/learner.tftest.hcl); replace the comment-only scaffold with **Ctrl+A**, **Ctrl+V**.
5. Keep the mock source, plan-time override, and all supplied default inputs. Read [tests/mocks/network.tfmock.hcl](../../tests/mocks/network.tfmock.hcl) to see the realistic synthetic IDs it loads.
6. Set the negative run's CIDR to the invalid value below; this is the complete expected learner file, not just two names to insert into comments:

```hcl
mock_provider "azurerm" {
  source          = "./tests/mocks"
  override_during = plan
}

variables {
  name                = "ws2-network"
  resource_group_name = "rg-ws2-existing"
  location            = "southeastasia"
  address_space       = ["10.42.0.0/16"]
  subnets = {
    web  = { address_prefixes = ["10.42.1.0/24"] }
    data = { address_prefixes = ["10.42.2.0/24"] }
  }
  tags = { owner = "team", environment = "dev", cost_center = "training", workshop = "ws2" }
}

run "learner_valid_subnets" {
  command = plan
  assert {
    condition     = toset(keys(output.subnet_ids)) == toset(["data", "web"])
    error_message = "Keep exactly the two caller-supplied subnet keys."
  }
}

run "learner_reject_invalid_cidr" {
  command = plan
  variables {
    address_space = ["10.300.0.0/16"]
  }
  expect_failures = [var.address_space]
}
```

7. Remove all `TODO` text and press **Ctrl+S**. Add no alternate-module test block, provider alias, real provider, or changed validation.

### 5. Execute the two cases for the right reason

1. In the repository-root terminal, run one line at a time and stop on an unexpected error:

```powershell
terraform fmt -check -recursive
terraform init -backend=false -lockfile=readonly -input=false
terraform validate
terraform test '-filter=tests\learner.tftest.hcl'
```

On macOS/Linux replace the last line with this native slash variant:

```bash
terraform test '-filter=tests/learner.tftest.hcl'
```

2. Quote the **whole** Windows `-filter=` argument. Confirm **two executed, passing runs**, including `learner_reject_invalid_cidr`; zero tests never count.
3. The second run passes because `var.address_space` rejects the invalid CIDR, not because authentication or another unrelated operation fails.

> [!WARNING]
> No Azure login, real backend, state access, or real plan/apply is allowed. Initial mock setup may download the locked provider, but it does not deploy.
> The full helper will still require the corrected sample and generated documentation from later steps; do not weaken it to pass early.

### 6. Review, stage, commit, publish, and inspect the newest commit

1. Press **Ctrl+Shift+G**, inspect the learner-test diff, select **+** (**Stage Changes**), and review **Staged Changes**.
2. Enter `lab: add valid subnet and invalid CIDR tests` in **Message**, select **Commit**, then **Publish Branch** to your existing private-copy `origin`.
3. Use **...** → **Push** for subsequent corrections; never publish another repository or force-push to fix a gate.
4. Refresh **your own GitHub copy**, select `lab/tests-docs` in **Code**, and inspect its newest commit and learner test file.
5. Open **Actions** → **Lab checks** → that newest-commit run → **Test learner module** → the learner-check command log; read its actual first diagnostic.
6. An unfinished rule fixture or documentation gate may still fail full CI. Refresh the Exercise **body** after **AgentAlvine** finishes to continue.

### Expected result, checks, and recovery

AgentAlvine requires the mock provider, exact run names `learner_valid_subnets` and `learner_reject_invalid_cidr`, `output.subnet_ids`, and `expect_failures = [var.address_space]`, without `TODO`, at a pushed revision.
The final gate also executes these cases. File text alone, a local success claim, or a copied screenshot is insufficient.
If the selector reports `Unknown test file`, check native separators and the exact learner path; if inputs are missing, restore the complete starter context, not live credentials.
For a real edit: **Ctrl+P** to the learner test, correct it, **Ctrl+S**, inspect/stage/commit through **Ctrl+Shift+G**, then **...** → **Push** and inspect the new run.

**Next action:** keep `lab/tests-docs` and open [Step 2: observe the detector and narrow the sample](02.md).
